questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not too far away both physically and culturally and I knew people would speak english well. Also I had been to Amsterdam before so not everything would be new.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a really good experience!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty easy. Got e-mails with all the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The people in charge of housing were there to give me the keys for my room. Also there was a whole introduction week with activities organized by the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I paid a fee to get the chance to get a room through the university. It ended up being a really good idea since I got a room only 10 min from the university. They distribute the rooms according to when you pay the fee so it is a good idea to do it as quick as possible. I felt like I was a bit late but luckily it worked out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure if you would call where I lived it on or off campus. I was staying in the green tower in Uilenstede where I shared a kitchen with 13 other exchange students and otherwise had my own room and bathroom. This was a really good option since the rent was also not very high (ca. 3.300 kr./month).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You need to be prepared to not have the most clean kitchen since not everyone is good at cleaning up after themselves. Otherwise I'm happy that I stayed there and the closest friends I made were my flatmates. It is also different from floor to floor if people are very social or not. If you want to live a very social place also the red tower at Uilenstede is a good option, but there you don't have your own bathroom.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember everything but you pretty much just need to apply and register for the courses you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always send questions to the staff if you had any questions. Also all the course descriptions are available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions you get, then everything should work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was not as high as at home but that is great when you want the time to experience the city or do stuff with your friends.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was mainly lectures and in some of the courses also lab work. I also had a few assignments (both alone and in grups) which I'm not used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The minor consisted of 5 courses:
Experimental cell biologi I and II, From protein to cell, Metabolomics and molecular microbiology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Experimental cell biology I and II were pretty basic courses and not a lot of new information. Also the lectures were kind of random and not always well connected. I liked the 3 other courses more and these were also courses where we did work in the lab. From protein to cell was nice beacuse there wasn't an exam but I think metabolomics and molecular microbiology were the most interesting of the courses.

questions.answer: I had to get a dutch number.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could get a membership at the sports center in Uilenstede. I didn't do it personally because I did something else, but a lot of people did and it seemed nice. There you can join a lot of different classes and sports (yoga, dance, fencing, kick boxing, basketball, volleyball) or you can go to the gym by yourself. I also heard that you can get a work out program from a "personal" coach if you wanted to.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think it as a really good idea to do some kind of activity in your free time. It is a great way to meet people and also super fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see some of the other cities in the Netherlands. E.g. Utricht, Zaandam, Den Haag, Delft) and go to some of the museums.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy since it's so similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I got to do group work in almost all the courses with dutch students and that was really nice. Since i was living with only exchange students I didn't meet a lot of local students. I also joined a sports club in Amsterdam where I met a lot of dutch people but if you don't force yourself to meet them you will not have a lot of activities with the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Can't really think of any. You have to adapt to the fact that you are living with people from a lot of different cultures though.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone speaks english pretty well and it is similar to Denmark in a lot of ways. It was also fun that a lot of words in dutch actually are the same in Danish.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to meet people and in the beginning you should also seek the opportunities to do stuff with other people because the friends you make in the beginning will most likely be the closest friends while you're away.
And enjoy it! The exchange is over before you know it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and also just the whole experience of living in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To say goodbye to the people at home and saying goodbye to the people I met when the exchange was over.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
